blocks.html: Each section on this page is a CSS grid with 24 columns on desktop and 8 on phones. Each block stores where it starts and where it ends. Drag a block, pull a handle, or double-click text to edit it.
24 columns and two gutter tracks

The grid has 26 tracks. The outer two are gutters, so a block can start at line 1 or end at line 27 and reach the edge of the window. The 24 tracks between them are capped at the site max width, so content stays centered on wide screens.
Rows scale with the width

On desktop the smallest a row can be is the container width times 0.0215. A 1400px container gives rows of 30.1px. On phones rows start at a fixed 24px.

Row height follows the width, so a layout keeps its proportions when the window changes.

When the window gets narrower this paragraph wraps onto more lines than its rows hold. The browser stretches those rows to fit the text, and everything below moves down. Start a drag anywhere in this section and the editor first converts the stretched rows back into uniform rows, so every snap moves the same distance.
On the published page the stretch stays. That is how text wraps on narrow screens without any JavaScript.
Blocks may share cells. The z-index decides which one is in front. Select a block and use Bring forward or Send backward.

Drag a block to move it. The blue area shows where it will land. Pull one of the 8 handles to resize. A text block cannot get shorter than its text. Arrow keys move the selected block one cell. Esc cancels a drag. Cmd+Z undoes it.
Double-click this text and add a few lines. The block grows by whole rows instead of stretching them.

Content is shared. Placement is not. Each block has one area for desktop and one for phones, and each section has a row count for each. Switch to the phone view and move these tiles. The desktop layout stays as it is.
The published page is HTML and CSS. Each section ships a style tag generated from the layout. No JavaScript moves blocks on the live site.
.fe-section { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(var(--grid-gutter), 1fr) repeat(24, minmax(0, var(--cell-max-width))) minmax(var(--grid-gutter), 1fr); }
